messages:
maria: FYI - customer acme-prod is seeing backfill failures from the vector indexer. getting a bunch of "dimension mismatch" rejects during ingest.

alex: Ugh. Do we have the exact error from the indexer? stack trace or sample payload?

maria: Paste from support logs: 
```
ERROR indexer.insert batch_id=bf-2026-03-17 failed: vector_dim_mismatch: expected_dim=1536 got_dim=1024 doc_ids=[...]
Detail: first bad vector: [0.0012, -0.0033, ...] length=1024
```

carla: That screams model swap. We rolled a new embed model last night in hosted for prod: redwood-embed-compact (1024) replaced redwood-embed-standard (1536) for the /v1/embeddings default.

jordan: Did the backfill pipeline pin the model? If some workers use old model and some the new one, we'll get mixed dims in the same batch.

ingest-sre: Confirming — the backfill job was kicked off at 02:10 UTC with the pipeline config referencing `model: default-embeddings` (not a concrete model id). After the staged model switch, some pool nodes started resolving to the compact model. Mixed outputs hit the indexer.

support-bot: Ticket #INC-2489 created for acme-prod. Priority: P1. Notifying SRE and Ingest.

alex: Immediate mitigation: stop the backfill job, and temporarily pause writes to the indexer for that customer. We should also pin model version in the pipeline config before resuming.

maria: Agreed. Paused the backfill at 12:04. Customer notified. They reported increased billing because retries were firing (~5000 failed attempts). Billing ops looped in.

carla: For the postmortem: need to require explicit model ids in long-running jobs (backfill, async pipelines). Defaults may change during a deployment.

jordan: Short repro to validate embedding dim quickly:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-compact","input":"test"}' | jq '.data[0].embedding | length'
```
Expect 1024 for compact, 1536 for standard.

alex: Also added a lightweight pre-check in the indexer: if batch contains mixed vector lengths, reject whole batch with clearer log and do not increment downstream offsets. That prevents partial progress and hidden corruption.

ingest-sre: Backfill plan:
- 1) pin pipeline to redwood-embed-standard (1536) to match existing vectors
- 2) restart backfill workers with pinned config
- 3) run a validator job to scan the queued batches for any mixed-dim batches and surface doc ids
- 4) for batches that already failed, re-embed and re-run insert into a staging index then swap
Estimated time: 3-6 hours depending on remaining docs.

carla: For long term: add a CI/gate that prevents a default-model rollout if there are active long-running jobs referencing the default alias. Also expose a pin option in the Console for running jobs.

maria: Support note for the customer: "We've paused your backfill to avoid further rejects and billing retries. We're preparing a targeted re-run that will preserve your existing vector dimensionality. ETA 4 hours. You will not be billed for failed retries — billing team is handling crediting."

alex: Quick tool to find bad batches (python one-liner):
```
python -c "import json;print([d['id'] for d in json.load(open('batch.json')) if len(d['vector']) not in (1024,1536)])"
```
Use to triage any saved failed batch dumps.

jordan: Postfix actions: update ops runbook, add metric for percentage of batches with mixed dims, and alert when >0.

maria: Thanks all — moving to action items. I published the pinned config in the pipeline repo and kicked off the validator. Will update once staging re-ingest completes. :thumbsup:

ingest-sre: Validator run found 47 mixed-dim batches (IDs in /sre/backfills/acme-2065432109-report.csv). Re-ingest started to staging index.

carla: Great work. Let's do a retro TOMORROW to lock the process.

maria: Closing the live incident channel when re-ingest is done. Leaving ticket open until swap is verified.
